t:
(a) In General.—Subparagraph (C) of section 621(a)(1) of the Adam Walsh Child Protection and Safety Act of 2006 (42 U.S.C. 16981(a)(1)) is amended to read as follows:“(C) Minimum standards.—The electronic monitoring units used in the pilot program shall at a minimum—“(i) provide a tracking device for each offender that contains a central processing unit with global positioning system; and“(ii) permit continuous monitoring of offenders 24 hours a day.”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by subsection (a) shall apply to grants provided on or after the date of the enactment of this Act.

fable.w: The section only sets minimum technical standards (GPS tracking, 24-hour monitoring) for electronic monitoring units in a pilot program and gives an effective date tied to grants. The tempting reading is that the grant program brings in states or local governments as grantees, but receiving or applying for a grant is not participation in a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
fable.s: The amendment made by subsection (a) shall apply to grants provided on or after the date of the enactment of this Act.

qwen_block.w: This section amends technical standards for electronic monitoring devices used in a pilot program and specifies the effective date for grants. It does not involve consultation with, or participation by, any non-federal entities in the decision-making process. The mention of 'grants' refers to the funding mechanism itself, not an application process or public participation requirement.
qwen_block.s: The amendment made by subsection (a) shall apply to grants provided on or after the date of the enactment of this Act.

opus.w: This section only sets minimum technical standards for electronic monitoring units in a grant-funded pilot program and gives an effective date. The mention of grants might suggest that outside grantees are involved, but receiving or applying for grants is expressly not participation. Nothing here requires a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or a right to sue.
opus.s: The amendment made by subsection (a) shall apply to grants provided on or after the date of the enactment of this Act.
opus.b:
**Step 1 – Analysis.** The tempting reading is that this section involves outside parties because it mentions a "pilot program" and "grants," and grantees such as states or localities sit outside the federal government. That reading fails. The section only sets minimum technical standards for electronic monitoring units (GPS tracking and 24-hour monitoring) and says when the amendment takes effect. Nobody outside the government is consulted, no comment period or hearing is required, no advisory body is created, and no right to sue is granted. Under the definition, receiving or applying for grants is not participation.

**Step 2 – Label.**

qwen_chat.w: The section amends technical standards for electronic monitoring devices and sets an effective date for grants. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by parties outside the federal government. The reference to grants is excluded from the definition of participation, and no advisory bodies or public comment periods are mentioned.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section amends a statute regarding a "pilot program" and "grants," it implies some form of public participation or consultation. However, the text itself only defines technical standards for electronic monitoring devices and sets an effective date for grants. It does not describe any process for consulting with outsiders, holding hearings, or forming advisory committees. The mention of "grants" falls under the exclusion for "applications for benefits or grants," and there is no language requiring interaction with non-federal entities in the decision-making process described here.
